Q: Why does swapping root.left and root.right using a temporary variable work, but a seemingly equivalent approach fails? A:

First example

In your first example you assign tmp left node of the root.

Then you assign right node of root to left node of the root. This makes that both, root.left and root.right point to the same object, that was referenced by root.right at the beginning.

At last, you assign to root.right reference of tmp, that was pointing to original root.left node, so now root.right references that.

And that concludes swap - root.left references object that was references by root.right and vice versa.

Second exampe

You assign to tmp value of root, so they both point to the same object.

So when you do root.right = tmp.left is effectively changing right node to left node in both tmp and root.

After that tmp as well as root have their right node updated.

So last line root.left = tmp.right does nothing, as left and right nodes reference now the same object.

Q: Java -- Round money to 2 decimal places A:

Math.round

Call Math.round to do rounding.

retail_price = Math.round(retail_price * 100.0) / 100.0;

Q: Format decimal to string in correct culture info A:

Add a format to the ToString: myDecimal.ToString("#.00") or myDecimal.ToString("C").

For a nullable decimal (decimal?) you will need to use the .Value property (myNullableDecimal.Value.ToString("C")) or cast the value to a plain (non-nullable) decimal. Be sure not to do this when the value is null or you will get an exception!

And if you don't mind showing a null value as 0.00, use myNullableDecimal.GetValueOrDefault().ToString("#.00"). Then you will not get exceptions on a null value (but 0.00).

See the documentation for Standard or Custom numeric format strings.

Q: Is there an easy way of seeing PHP info? A:

From your command line you can run..

php -i

I know it's not the browser window, but you can't see the phpinfo(); contents without making the function call.

Another approach would be to have a PHP script in the root of your web server directory that calls phpinfo();, that way you have access to it at all times via http://localhost/info.php or something similar. However, this is not suitable for a production environment unless you ensure that you secure it.

Update: As mentioned by binaryLV, its quite common to have two versions of a php.ini per installation. One for the command line interface (CLI) and the other for the web server interface. If you want to see phpinfo output for your web server make sure you specify the ini file path, for example...

php -c /etc/php/apache2/php.ini -i
